endings._about: D-053: the endings and the endpoint's own checks as ONE table, its rows in the order they happen, derived from the paths' chains. The moments and the two options are my picks where the ruling left the look open (D-025.2).
endings.plain: The endings in the order they happen, read off the paths' chains: on every path an ending it checks earlier stands above one it checks later, and an ending a path checks twice stands where it is first checked. Where no path orders a pair of endings, the stage the chains show first comes first, then the handler line that reaches the ending (one raised inside a call stands at the line of that call), then its own line. The uncaught ending stands last: an error nobody catches can escape at any moment, so it has no place of its own in time.
endings.plainInput: INPUT appears twice here. FastAPI reads the body before the login check runs, so a body it cannot read ends above the gate; it checks the endpoint's own fields after the login check, so a field that does not fit ends below it.
endings.plainInputFirst: Here a field check stands above the login check: FastAPI checks a dependency's own parameters before it runs that dependency, and does not run it when one does not fit. The endpoint's own fields are checked after the login check; an ending checked at both moments stands where it is first checked.
endings.plainChecks: Each of the endpoint's own checks stands on the row of the ending it produces. A row that shared code decides (the app band, the login check, FastAPI) names who decides it, drawn apart: it is not a check the endpoint wrote, and a check a dependency makes is drawn muted beside it. A success carries no check, because it is what is left when every check passed; an uncaught ending carries none either, because no check makes it. The handler's rows split into the moments they happen at: its own checks, and what follows when a call it made raised, one group for each catch that caught it. A group names the calls that raise into its catch; a call that only runs before the catch is not named, and a group that names none still says where the error was caught.
endings.plainUnplaced: A row that starts with a check inside a call holds a check whose ending the map does not name; it stands at the line where the handler makes that call.
endings.sharedPlain: Decided by code the endpoint shares with others, not by a check of its own.

lines: Every row comes from the lab's own reader: gen-endpoint-facts.py ran once per endpoint, into a temporary file, never over the lab's facts. This page keeps a small record of each and counts what the facts already say.
The feed is the forms file of {app} at head {head}, sha {formsSha}, with its map beside it, sha {archmapSha}. Arms on: {arms}. Arms off: {armsOff}.
A cell that reads absent means the feed did not look. A cell that reads unknown means it looked, and the value is not known. A zero means it looked and found nothing, and its hover says why.

The stage an ending leaves from follows the robot's lay: the app band's endings at the edge, the login check's at the gate, the body's at the input, the endpoint's own refusals in the handler, every success at the answer, and the uncaught in the bay.

The writes column and a path's fate read the endpoint's own writes only. The login check can create a user row on almost every endpoint; counting it would paint both columns the same, so the endpoint section names those writes apart, as the login check's.

mo._about: His ask 2026-09-26: are the moments universal, can every block be read on them. The spine, the moment words, the reasons and the path row are my proposals (D-025.2); the two looks' defaults, moments as columns and cells as chips, are his (D-055); where each element stands is read off the feed by gen-all-endpoints.py (by_moment) and proven there.
mo.lede: One endpoint's time, left to right, with every block as a row (his default; the other look turns it). A column is a moment of the request; a cell holds that block's elements acting at that moment. The last column, no moment, holds what is true of the endpoint at no moment of a request: what it is and what sums it up. Pick a code in the path row to follow only that path to its ending.
how: The moments are D-053's, extended. Before the handler they are fixed: the server starting (before any request), the screen sending the request, the app's edge, FastAPI reading the body, the dependencies (the login check among them), FastAPI checking the fields. Inside the handler they are read from its own lines: its checks, and what it does among them; the work, the calls it makes after a check and before its next check, catch or commit; one moment for each catch that turns a failure into an ending; saving, its own commit. Then the answer, what happens after it, and the uncaught error last, because it can escape at any moment.

A handler moment that happens twice (checks, then a catch, then more checks) is drawn twice, in the order it happens, never merged. The arms of one if and else are drawn the same way, as runs in line order, though a request passes only one of them: pick its ending to see which. A fixed moment the endpoint does not have is drawn empty where it would stand.

An element stands at the moment the map records for it: its stage, its line in the handler, or the handler call it runs inside. A check stands where it is evaluated: on the paths whose chain carries it, and for a check inside a call, on the paths that make that call, less those the map shows leaving before it (on a path it rides only by the call, its hover says a path may skip it); its ending stands where the request leaves. A check the map ties only to a catch stands where that catch raises its ending. A test has no time inside the request: it rides the ending it proves. What has no moment by nature stands in the last column, no moment; what should have a moment and the map cannot place is left in the band below, with its reason.

A step is placed once for each path it is on: with the dependencies when a dependency runs it, else at the call that path makes. So one step can stand at more than one moment: the login dependency reads a table, and a handler call reads it again. When a path's own chain names no call reaching the step, it stands at the calls the endpoint's other paths make to its function, never after that path has left.

The path: every path at once, or one path to its ending. Each path is a code, in the order its ending happens, a small gap between the moments they leave at; an ending several paths reach is several codes, told apart by the fork each takes, else by what FastAPI checks on it. A code's hover says the fork, the moment, what the ending says, its limiter, and whether it is the path in force. A picked path keeps only the moments it passes and the elements it passes there; an ending it passes by without leaving is kept.

A moment's head says little: a handler moment after a call failed names the function the map shows raising (when it names one) and the class its except takes; the checks say so; the work names the first function it calls, and how many more; saving names what the handler's own step does there. Its full name, where the catch stands, its lines and its stage are in its hover.

With one path picked, a write wears what that path does with it: saved, maybe saved, rolled back or left unsaved. An ending's status is drawn hollow when the endpoint does not declare it. A test whose status fits endings at several moments rides each of them, its chip hollow and dashed. A function behind the handler stands at the handler call that reaches it, the arrow saying how many calls below the handler it is, on the paths of the function it hangs under, less the paths the map shows leaving before it: a fork that returns, or a check that fires first, in the function that calls it (the rule a check inside a call follows); a call written inside an except stands only on the paths that enter that except. One the map reaches through no call stands where a function placed at a moment names it behind it (the Gabe Universe's behind lists), on that function's paths; its hover names any placed function whose list is cut that may also run it. One no placed function names stands in the band, and so does one that functions at different moments name. A raise called before it counts as a leaving point too, where the path's chain fires that raise or its ending was read to it. Where the map records no line the function is called at, no path can be dropped from it: on a path that leaves the function it hangs under partway, or that an error from the handler call ends with no line the map names for its raise, its hover says it may never be called there; where that function's own paths are an upper bound, its hover says so, naming the same call. A function called only inside an except the map records no path entering, while the uncaught 500 passes an error on through that except, stands in the band, on the way to the 500.

The last column, no moment, holds per block the facts no moment of a request holds: what the endpoint is (its method and path, the path it is served at, its first segment, its entity and the cluster the Gabe Universe draws it in, the station's flags, the handler's file with the line its route is declared at and the line its def stands at, its outline, its docstring) and what sums it up (how many functions stand behind it, its proof, its alarms, each path's fate, its longest path, the cases that only arrange through it, its rare pieces that name what it is, the norms it lacks), each in the row of the block it belongs to. The path row never hides it: each fact is true of every path.

edge.name: at the edge

body.name: reads the body
body.plain: FastAPI reads the request's body before any dependency runs.

fields.name: checks the fields

checks.name: checks
checks.plain: The handler's own checks, and what it does among them.

work.name: the work
work.plain: The calls the handler makes after its checks, and what they read and write inside.

fail.name: after a call failed
fail.plain: A call raised; this catch turned the error into these endings.

answer.plain: The handler returns; FastAPI checks the reply against its model and sends it.

after.plain: What runs once the answer has left: a stream's own code, and what the screen does with the answer.

uncaught.name: escapes
uncaught.plain: An error nobody catches can escape at any moment, so it stands last.

path.label: the path
path.allPlain: Every path at once: each element wherever it acts.
path.pickIt: click to follow only this path

rows.name: moments as rows
rows.plain: Time runs top to bottom; each block is a column.

cols.plain: Time runs left to right; each block is a row.

nm._about: D-064 (2), his ruling 2026-09-28: the facts no moment holds, per block, as the table's last column (the last row when the moments are rows). Its place at the end, its name and these words are my proposal; which facts stand there, and in which block's row, is read from the ruled tree's homes by gen-all-endpoints.py (no_moment) and proven there. `only` names the blocks whose every fact has no moment.
nm.name: no moment
nm.plain: What is true of the endpoint at no moment of a request: what it is and what sums it up. Each fact is true of every path, so the path row never hides it.

ep.name: method and path
ep.plain: The verb and the URL a client calls.

full.name: the path it is served at
full.plain: The path the app answers it on: its own path, with its router's mount before it.

seg.name: the URL's first segment
seg.plain: The first part of its path: the group of URLs it sits in.
seg.label: the map labels its path {v}; the segment is read from the path it is served at

ent.name: entity
ent.plain: The feature of the app that owns the endpoint.

cl.name: cluster
cl.plain: The group of endpoints the Gabe Universe draws it in, inside its entity.
cl.label: the Gabe Universe groups it by the path the map labels it with, {v}

risk.name: flag
risk.plain: A warning the Gabe Universe draws on the endpoint.

untested.plain: No test calls the endpoint: no case acts on it and none sets another test up through it.

conflict.plain: A large surface: many functions stand behind the handler, or many pieces lead to it, so a change here reaches far.

god.plain: Its handler is one of the app's oversized functions or classes.

behind.name: functions behind
behind.plain: How many functions the handler's own calls reach, and how many calls below it the deepest one stands; the functions its dependencies run are not counted (the Functions row draws them at the moment the dependencies run).

proof.name: proof
proof.plain: How many of its refusals a test names, and where that puts the endpoint among the app's.

alarm.name: alarm
alarm.plain: An anomaly the form check found; the facts it reads stand at their moments.

file.name: the handler's file and line
file.plain: The file the handler lives in, and the line its route is declared at: its decorator, which stands above the def. The line the def stands at is beside it when it is known.

sig.name: the handler's outline
sig.plain: Async or not, how many lines it runs, the type it returns; its def in the hover.

doc.name: the handler's docstring
doc.plain: The text the handler's author wrote at its top.

fate.name: each path's fate
fate.plain: What becomes of the endpoint's own writes, path by path, counted: saved, maybe saved, rolled back, left unsaved, after the answer, or no write of its own.

chain.name: the longest path
chain.plain: How many steps the longest path a request can take runs through.

arr.name: arranges another test
arr.plain: A case that calls this endpoint only to set another test up. A test has no time inside the request, and this one proves no ending here.

piece.name: a rare piece
piece.plain: A piece few endpoints carry that names what the endpoint is (its method, its login, its limit), not something that acts.

lack.name: a norm it lacks
lack.plain: A piece nearly every endpoint carries that this one does not.

nolink.name: no link to a call
nolink.plain: The map records no link from it to a call the handler makes, so where it happens inside the request is not known.

twomom.name: calls at different moments
twomom.plain: It is reached from handler calls that stand at different moments.

notable.name: no step
notable.plain: The map says the endpoint touches this table, but no step it records says when.

firstcall.name: filled on a first call
firstcall.plain: Its value is built by whichever request calls it first, and no one can say which.

spans.name: several moments
spans.plain: The endings it stands for leave at several moments, so it has no single one.

member.name: a member has no moment
member.plain: It stands for endings or catches, and one of them has no moment of its own.

noend.name: proves no ending
noend.plain: The test sends the request but none of its assertions fits an ending.

nosite.name: outside the handler
nosite.plain: It stands at a line outside the handler's own code, and no call of the handler is recorded for it.

pathsonly.name: paths only
pathsonly.plain: The map says which paths it is on, but not where on them.

fnnone.name: no call reaches it
fnnone.plain: The map names the function, but records no handler call that reaches it.

swmoves.name: moves with the path
swmoves.plain: Its paths place it at different moments.

nopath.name: on no path
nopath.plain: The endpoint lists it, but none of its paths passes it, so no path can be followed to it.

noname.name: by name only
noname.plain: It is named behind the handler, and no single function carries the name, so no call can be followed to it; and no function placed at a moment names it behind it.

in500.name: on the way to the 500
in500.plain: It is called inside an except that passes the error on. The only way into that except the map knows ends in the uncaught 500, and the map does not follow that path through the handler's calls, so it has no moment to give it.

x._about: D-056: what each element's hover adds, read off the feed (the operator's twelve adds, his ruling "agree with your recommendations").
x.depthPlain: How many calls below the handler it is reached.
x.callPathsPlain: It runs inside {via}, and a path may leave {via} before it runs, so a path picked here may not reach it.
x.cutNearPlain: {v} calls more functions than are listed; if this is one of them, it also runs where {v} runs, on its paths.
x.callCheck: checked inside {via}; a path picked here may skip it
x.callCheckPlain: It stands on the paths that call {via}, less those that leave {via} before it; a path may still skip it or leave before it, so a path picked here may not reach it.
x.leftIn: this path leaves {via} partway, maybe before calling it
x.leftInAll: on {n} of its paths, {via} is left partway, maybe before calling it
x.leftInPlain: It is called somewhere inside {via}. A path that leaves {via} partway, at a check that fires or on an error, may leave before that call, so it may never run on that path.
x.fatePlain: With one path picked, a write wears what the path does with it.
x.racePlain: A first call and its retry with the same key both pass the check before this step; the later one breaks the unique key ({cols}) of {tbl} here, nothing catches it, and it ends in the uncaught {st}.
x.declaredPlain: The endpoint declares this status: the decorator's success status, a declared refusal, or the 422 FastAPI declares for every endpoint it checks.
x.undeclaredPlain: The endpoint does not declare this status; a client reading its contract does not expect it.
x.hollow: fits {n} endings; this is one of them

x.file: a file, not a hook or component inside it
x._d057: D-057 (his ruling "build 1 and 2"): a check says the error it raises and its words (a); a client branch what it reads and what it does (b); an error nothing catches its cause, on the 500 and on the function it is raised in (e)

x.uncaught: raises {cls} at {at}, and nothing catches it

mo.noCode: No refusal this app sends carries a code of its own ({nCoded} of its {nRefusals}): a client tells one refusal from another by the status and the words alone.

carry._about: D-055: his ask 2026-09-26, a switch in the code map that dims or hides every field BY MOMENT already carries, to see what else is there. Its three looks and the default (show all) are my proposal (D-025.2): the default is my pick, dashed. What counts as carried is read by gen-all-endpoints.py (carried) and proven there.
carry.label: what BY MOMENT carries

all.name: show all
all.plain: Every field of the code map, as it is.

dim.name: dim what BY MOMENT carries
dim.plain: An element BY MOMENT places at a moment fades; a field whose elements it places, every one, fades with its name. Pointing at one brings it back. A field with nothing on this endpoint fades too, less; a field that lists fewer tables than BY MOMENT's steps touch stays and says how many more.

hide.name: hide what BY MOMENT carries
hide.plain: An element BY MOMENT places leaves the code map; a field it carries whole leaves with its name; a field it carries in part says how many of its elements are there. A field with nothing on this endpoint stays, faded; a field that lists fewer tables than BY MOMENT's steps touch stays and says how many more.

carry.count: {covered} of {fields} fields carried by BY MOMENT · {left} left · {empty} with nothing here
carry.tipAll: BY MOMENT carries this field whole: each of its elements stands at a moment there.
carry.tipPart: BY MOMENT carries {n} of its {of} elements.
carry.tipEmpty: This field holds nothing on this endpoint: nothing for BY MOMENT to carry, and nothing it leaves out. Dim and hide fade it, and the header counts it apart.
carry.tipBeyond: BY MOMENT's steps also touch {n} tables this field does not list: {names}. The code map is short of them.
carry._aboutPanels: D-058: his ruling 2026-09-26, the same switch in the Gabe Universe and in THE GAPS, one per panel, each remembered apart. The names and the default are the code map's (D-055: show all is my pick, dashed); what each panel reads as carried is gen-all-endpoints.py's panels_carried, on carried()'s own join, proven there.
carry.pcount: {carried} of {items} carried by BY MOMENT · {left} left

opts.all: Every row of the universe card, as it is.
opts.dim: An item BY MOMENT draws at a moment fades: a guard, a table, a chip, a case, found by its key, or a function Code behind names without one, found by its name. A row whose items it draws, every one, fades with its title. Pointing at one brings it back.
opts.hide: An item BY MOMENT draws leaves the card; a row whose items it draws, every one, leaves with its title; a row it draws in part says how many of its items are there.

uni.plain: Carried, on the universe card: an item BY MOMENT draws at a moment, on any path, or in its last column, found by the key the code map's switch reads, or, for a function Code behind names without a key, by its name (when that name is one function there); a table an access or a connection reads or writes, by a chip of that same op (a read never carries a write); the endpoint is BY MOMENT's heading. A count or a line (the usage, the fields a payload ferries, a file's cases, the layer, the fan-in) stays unless the card names every member it counts and BY MOMENT draws each one; the cluster, the signature, the docstring, a flag and the count behind are carried by BY MOMENT's last column, which draws them. What BY MOMENT holds only in its band, not placed, is not carried.
uni.tipAll: BY MOMENT draws every item of this row.
uni.tipPart: BY MOMENT draws {n} of its {of} items.

opts.dim: A gap BY MOMENT already carries fades: a name it draws at a moment; an attribute of the universe card whose items it draws, every one; an attribute of the code map whose fields it carries whole. A block of such gaps fades with its head. Pointing at one brings it back.
opts.hide: A gap BY MOMENT already carries leaves; a block it carries whole leaves with its head; a block or an attribute it carries in part says how many are there.

gaps.plain: The switch reads whichever way the gaps are shown. From the code map: an attribute is carried when every code-map field that holds it is carried whole, as the code map's own switch reads it; a field with nothing here is passed over, and a field that sums the endpoint up is one element, carried when BY MOMENT's last column draws it. From the universe: a name is carried when BY MOMENT draws every item of the card it names (a journey with the entities it crosses, a table's read and its write); an attribute when BY MOMENT draws every item of the row that holds it; a row that maps to no attribute when it draws every item of that row.
gaps.tipAll: BY MOMENT already carries all of it.
gaps.tipPart: BY MOMENT carries {n} of its {of} elements.

carry.plain: Carried: an element BY MOMENT places at a moment, on any path, or a fact one of its elements draws. A table read is carried by a chip that reads it, a table written by one that writes it. A list carries each of its items apart: an alarm when every fact it reads stands at its moment, a path's fate when its writes wear it on its pick (or it writes nothing of its own). A count is carried when every member it counts is placed, in part when some are. A field that sums the whole endpoint up (the count of the fates, the alarms' dots, the longest chain, the count behind, the proof's rank) is carried by BY MOMENT's last column, no moment, which draws it; so is what the endpoint is there (its entity, the handler's file, the cases that only arrange through it, the norms it lacks). A field with nothing on this endpoint is counted apart, never as left. Where BY MOMENT's steps touch tables the code map does not list, the tables fields stay in every look and say how many, and the header counts them.

authNoSchemePlain: It asks for a login through its own check, with no declared scheme: the check reads the token itself, not from the usual header.

one.lede: The endpoint picked in the table, read side by side. Left, the card the Gabe Universe draws for it today, row by row. Right, what the code map knows about it, under the card's blocks. In the middle, the gaps between them.

gaps.plain: Attributes of the card the code map holds something for here, that no row of the universe card shows, then those it shows only part of. A zero, an empty list, absent or unknown does not count as holding something.

status._about: D-044: every item of THE GAPS says in its hover WHY the gap exists (D-042's reasons, read by _ae_universe.gap_whys through why_of — never typed per item) and a STATUS: solved elsewhere (a link lights the code-map field that holds it) · not solving (and what keeps it off, a D-nnn cited) · open (what the code map's data would have to carry, and where from; or, with no plan, the measurement owed). `table` is MY PROPOSAL, keyed by (dir, at, why, q): dir a = in the code map, not in the universe · b = the other way; at = an attribute id (a) or "<kind of element | the thing a row draws | attribute> @ <ROW>", or a ROW alone (b); why = the item's FIRST reason; q = a word the forms feed decides (where it holds a case · a schema nested or not) or whether the row draws anything for an attribute (drawn · none drawn) — an entry without q answers every q. The build stops when a gap on the full page finds no line, or a line lines no gap.
status.minePlain: What each gap's status says is my proposal, not a ruling: one table, keyed by the gap's place and its first reason, tabled under more information at the end of the page. The reasons are D-042's, derived; only the status lines are written.

solved.plain: The code map holds it another way; the link lights the field that holds it.

not.name: not solving
not.plain: It stays off, for the reason and the ruling the line cites.

open.name: open
open.plain: What the code map's data would have to carry, and where from; or, where there is no plan yet, the measurement owed.

gap.name: not drawn
gap.plain: No row of the universe card draws it for this endpoint.

status.plain: Pointing at a gap says why it exists, in D-042's words, and then its status, my proposal: solved elsewhere (a link lights the field that holds it; move onto the hover to use it), not solving (and the ruling that keeps it off), or open (what the code map's data would have to carry, and where from, or the measurement owed).
status.count: Across the page's endpoints: {nStSolved} gaps solved elsewhere · {nStNot} not solving · {nStOpen} open.

enc._about: D-043: in ONE ENDPOINT's code-map column every action word and every value from a fixed set is a chip that carries a colour and/or an icon, its words its aria-label and its hover. REUSE FIRST — `col`/`ico`/`txt` name where a family's colour, icon and chip text are read: `table` = the page's own tokens and classes (the endings slots --k-*, the stage spine, the fate stack --f-*, the pieces stack --p-*, the method colours --m-*, the alarm dots' --alert, the validation slot's colour); `lab` = the endpoint lab's source, cut out of _lab-ep-panels.js and run under node with the station's tokens by gen-all-endpoints.py (the channel chip R · W · RW and its .jdrw rule in _lab-ep.css, the five path kinds' glyphs, the status colour rule — the lab colours a 3xx as it colours a 5xx, kept as the lab has it — the in-flight kinds' glyphs and lifetime tones, the direction chip IN · OUT, the words for what a branch does); `station` = the Gabe Universe's own encoding (D-052): a family an element wears as its subcategory (method · role · hook role · component, module and provider class · delivery) is the station's badge colour and word, lifted from gabe-universe.html by _ae_universe.station_kinds; the entity is the station's entity glyph in that entity's colour. A finding's hover words are the forms registry's own (_a3_forms.py FINDINGS). `mine` = MY PROPOSAL, for a family nothing encodes yet: an icon per value from the station's own icon set, and no new colour. `rule.groups[*].keywords` sorts the 422 rule types by the Field keyword that makes each (the short arm's PYDANTIC_ERRORS), `table` by the short arm's MODEL_ERRORS / RAISE_ERRORS — which group a keyword belongs to is my proposal; a keyword no group names stops the build.
enc.title: how the code map draws its values
enc.plain: Every action word and every value from a fixed set is a chip that carries a colour, an icon, or both. Point at one for its words. The looks, family by family, and where each is read from:

from.lab: as the endpoint lab draws it
from.station: as the Gabe Universe draws it

rw.name: reads and writes
rw.plain: The endpoint reads this table and writes it.

1.name: an informational status
1.plain: The server says it is still working on the request.

3.name: a redirect status
3.plain: The caller is sent somewhere else.

4.name: a client error status
4.plain: The request is refused; the caller can change it and try again.

5.name: a server error status
5.plain: The server failed; nothing the caller changes fixes it.

with the answer.plain: It is gone when the reply is sent: each request has its own.

with the server process.plain: It stays while the server runs: every request shares it.

unknown.plain: How long it lives is not read.

ent.name: entity
ent.plain: The entity that claims this endpoint, with the entity glyph in its own colour, as the Gabe Universe draws an entity.

binding.plain: Which implementation is plugged in decides the way.

value.plain: A setting's value decides the way.

flag.plain: A flag turns a way on or off.

branch.name: what the branch does with the reason

reads.plain: The branch reads the reason the endpoint gives.

passed.plain: The branch hands the error to code that reads it.

value.plain: The branch only picks a value.

none.plain: The branch uses neither the reason nor the error.

unread.plain: What the branch does is not read: its condition is too long.

_other.plain: What the branch does with the reason.

does.name: what the map read of the branch

read.plain: Read: the rows the branch runs are named.

mixed.plain: More than one check on a line shares these rows.

_other.plain: What the map read of the branch.

pattern.name: a pattern the text must match

model.name: a rule of the whole shape: a field required, a field not allowed, a value from a list

validator.name: a rule the app's own validator raises

limit.name: rate limiter
limit.plain: It lets this many requests through per window, then refuses.

universe._about: The universe column: the Gabe Universe's endpoint card, row by row. Each row's icon and title are LIFTED from the station's source by _ae_universe.py. `say` holds the station card's own words (templates/center/shell/gabe-universe.html), lifted so the values read as the station writes them. `rows[*].attrs` is MY PROPOSAL: which attributes of the card's ruled inventory each station row shows, every id checked against the tree and inventory-endpoint.md; the gaps column is computed from it. `rows[*].attrs` holds for every endpoint; a few attributes are also read per endpoint from what the card draws (_ae_universe.read_here), which one.gaps.perEp says on the page.

marks._about: The block marks on the table and in the endpoint section (D-036). A block the ruled tree pairs to a lab PART wears that part's icon and colour, read from the lab's registry, never from here. A block with no part wears THE LAB SECTION MAP'S mark for it, read from the lab's own source (_lab-ep-map.js blockMark, D-035): the command panel's glyph for Endings, the running header's for the block read across every part, the one no-page mark for the rest, each in the colour token the lab paints it. Those marks are my picks in the lab too, so they stay dashed. Only the Shared group's icon is picked here.
marks.part: the {v} part's icon and colour, from the lab
marks.pick: my pick: the Shared group has no part in the lab
marks.lab: the lab's section map marks it this way ({v}) — my pick there too, not ruled

pinRow: The endpoint picked in the table, pinned at the top with the column names. Click it to go to its section below.

el._about: D-041: click an element of information in the universe column or the code-map column and it lights in all three places. Keys and their aliases are read by gen-all-endpoints.py (key_index, keyspace); these are the words the light speaks.
el.noCol: no column of the table counts it
el.plain: Click an element in either column or in BY MOMENT (a chip, a pair, a list item, a name) and it lights everywhere it appears: the table rows whose endpoint holds it (the rest dim), the cells of the columns that count it, and every place either column or BY MOMENT draws it. A column, or BY MOMENT, that does not hold it says so at its top. Click it again, press Escape or clear to put it out; choosing another endpoint keeps it lit.
el.alias: Which things are one element is my reading. Every element carries one key ({nKeys} on this page). A model class and its database table are one element, joined by the station graph's model-to-table map and the forms feed's models ({nAlias} classes). A function is its file and qualified name; a callee name for which the feeds hold no single function carries no key and cannot be lit ({nUnkeyed} of {nNames} names). A name a condition reads is a setting of the forms feed, else a flag; a guard, a switch or an in-flight value holds the settings and flags its condition reads. A row is lit when its endpoint holds the element anywhere on this page: in the table, its universe card or its code map.

why._about: D-042: when the code map does not NAME a lit element, the code-map column's top line says why. The reasons are my reading of his ask, read by _ae_universe.cm_reasons from each row's keys and from `table` below — never typed per element. `table` is MY PROPOSAL: for each kind of element and the universe rows that draw it, the card's attributes it belongs to (ids of the ruled tree, checked against inventory-endpoint.md; an unknown id stops the build) and the code-map fields it can sit in (c:<column> · h:<head pair> · d:<detail pair>). A field the data shows holding it that the table does not list also stops the build. `about: map` marks a kind whose presence is a fact about the map (D-017).
why.head: {name} ({kind}) — not named in the code map

cnt.name: counted, not named
cnt.plain: A field of the code map counts it but does not name it. Pointing at the link lights that field; a click goes there and keeps it lit.

alt.name: shown another way
alt.plain: The same thing sits in another field of the code map, under another form or kind: a dependency as the value it hands in, a flag as the condition that reads it, a schema as the rules on it. Pointing at the link lights that field; a click goes there and keeps it lit.

low.name: low priority
low.plain: Every attribute it belongs to is rated {rLow} of {rTop} in the card's inventory: mentioned, never drilled. The card leaves it to a hover or to more information (D-020).

map.name: about the map, not the code
map.plain: It says how the map files or finds something, not what the code does, so it waits behind more information (D-017).

gap.name: not carried
gap.plain: The code map's data holds nothing of the kind for this endpoint: a real gap. The link turns THE GAPS to what the universe shows that the code map does not hold.

none.name: not on this endpoint
none.plain: Neither column draws it for this endpoint, so there is nothing here for the code map to name.

why.refTip: Pointing lights this field of the code map; a click goes there and keeps it lit until the light is put out.
why.plain: When the code map does not name a lit element, its top line says why, in my words, one reason or several. Counted, not named: a field counts it without naming it. Shown another way: the same thing sits in another field under another form or kind. Low priority: every attribute it belongs to is rated {rLow} of {rTop}, so the card leaves it to a hover or more information (D-020). About the map, not the code: it says how the map files or finds something (D-017). Not carried: the code map's data holds nothing of the kind here, a real gap. When neither column holds it here, the line says it is not on this endpoint. A reason that names a field links it: pointing lights the field, a click goes there and keeps it lit until the element's light is put out; the link of not carried turns THE GAPS to what the universe shows that the code map does not hold. Which attributes and fields each kind of element belongs to is my proposal, tabled under more information at the end of the page.
why.mine: Why the code map lacks a lit element is read from this table, my proposal, not a ruling: for each kind of element and the universe rows that draw it, the attributes of the card it belongs to and the fields of the code map it can sit in. A field the data shows holding it that the table does not list stops the build.
tableHead: fields of the code map it can sit in

station._about: D-052: every mention of an element the Gabe Universe draws as a node wears the station's glyph for its kind, in the station's kind colour, and, where the station hangs a badge on that kind, a small label at the END naming the subcategory in the badge's colour. Glyphs, colours, badge colours and their words are lifted from gabe-universe.html by _ae_universe.station_kinds (a table or a line that is gone stops the build). `map` is ONE table, MY PROPOSAL where a key's kind is not one of the station's node kinds (`mine`): `to` the station kind it is drawn as (`fe` = the piece's own kind in the station's frontend feed; `element` = only a file the station draws as an unclaimed-file node; null = the station draws no node for it, so it keeps the page's own look, D-043), `why` the reason. gen-all-endpoints.py checks every key kind has a row and every `to` is a kind the station's tables draw.
station.title: what the Gabe Universe draws
station.plain: An element the Gabe Universe draws as a node wears its glyph there, in its colour there; a label at the end names its subcategory, in the colour of the badge the station hangs on that node. Point at a glyph or a label for its words. Which of this page's kinds are drawn as which of the station's is my proposal where they are not the same:
station.drawn: as the Gabe Universe draws its node
station.drawnEnt: as the Gabe Universe names an entity
station.glyph: The glyph and the colour this kind of element wears in the Gabe Universe.
station.alias: The Gabe Universe names this setting as one of the flag's aliases, so it is that flag and wears the flag's glyph.
station.card: This is the node's look. The universe column copies the station's card, whose chips and entity faces use the card's own colours, so the same element can look different there: the station differs from itself.
station.nonode: The Gabe Universe draws no node for this function, so it wears no glyph; its role is read from the endpoint's facts the way the station reads a role.
station.same: The station's map gives these entities one colour: {v}.
station.count: {n} of {of} named here are nodes there
station.not: Not drawn by the Gabe Universe as a node, so each keeps this page's own look: {v}.

endpoint.why: The same: the station's endpoint node, its method and its delivery as labels.

fn.why: The station's function node, where its function layer holds the function, its role read from that layer. A function it holds no node for wears no glyph; its role stays as a label.

schema.why: The station's schema node, where its map holds the schema. A schema named only inside a signature is no node, so it wears no glyph.

flag.why: The station's feature flag node, where its map holds the flag.

table.why: A table and its model class are one element here (D-041); the station draws the model, where its map holds one for the table.

entity.why: The station draws an entity as the boundary round its pieces; where it names one (its panel, a search hit) it draws the entity glyph in that entity's own colour.

fe.why: A frontend piece is drawn as its own kind in the station's frontend feed; a component the station calls a view wears the screen glyph and the view colour.

file.why: The station draws a file as a node only when no entity claims it; any other file is no node.

guard.why: An own guard is a condition inside the handler; the station draws the endpoint's gates as its Guards list, never as a node.

setting.why: A setting is a value a condition reads; the station draws a node only for a feature flag. A setting the station names as one of a flag's aliases is that flag, and wears the flag's glyph.

limiter.why: A rate limiter lives inside the rate-limit middleware, which the station draws as one node for every request.

case.why: A test case sits on the card's Tests row, not as a node.

status.why: A status is a value, not a node.

fork.why: A deciding branch is a place in the code, not a node.

catch.why: A catch is a place in the code, not a node.

switch.why: A switch is what decides a way; the station draws none.

reason.why: A reason site is a line of a screen, not a node.

rule.why: A validation rule sits on a field of a schema, not as a node.

inflight.why: A value alive during a request is not a node.

finding.why: A finding is a fact about the endpoint, not a node.

piece.why: A piece is how common a shape is across the endpoints, not a node.
